acceptanceCriteria: The owner records which boundary applies to gate-ledger records.
If records must be self-consistent, lookup decodes strictly with a byte bound and treats a partial or unknown-field record as RUN, with a test.
body: Filed 2026-10-04 from the V1-0712 output-class inventory (docs/build-log/2026-10-04-v1-0712-output-class-inventory.md), source origin/main a2615609. Suspected defect, not confirmed as a contract violation; runtime NOT_RUN. ledger.lookup (tools/gate-ledger/main.go:776) reads the record with unbounded os.ReadFile, decodes it with lenient json.Unmarshal, and returns HIT when only Schema == gate-ledger/1 and Key match. A hand- or agent-written two-field file in the owner's 0700 ledger directory therefore skips that gate step. ledgerDirectory checks ownership, so the exposure is limited to processes already running as the owner, which includes agent sessions. Question: should lookup require the full record written by record() (strict decode, recorded command and outcome) and a byte bound, or is the owner-only directory the accepted boundary?

completion.reason: Criterion 1 met by beamfall/corvint#561, merged 2026-10-05T00:01:50Z as aa35f4bc via auto-merge: the owner-only gate-ledger record directory (GL-V0-006) is recorded as the accepted trust boundary in docs/specs/gate-ledger-v0.md (trust-boundary section) and docs/build-log/2026-10-04-v1-0744-gate-ledger-trust-boundary.md, which record the owner's 2026-10-04 'Owner-only dir' choice made in the session that delivered #561. Criterion 2 is conditional on records having to be self-consistent and does not apply under that decision. Evidence digests = sha256 at main aa35f4bc of the build-log entry and the spec. Doc-only disposition: code, requirements and tests unchanged; dogfood CEM NOT_PRODUCED (no code hunk); runtime NOT_RUN.
